text:
Local inference on Apple Silicon: what actually changed in 2026

For two years the advice was simple: buy more RAM. Unified memory let a 16 GB M1 Pro run a 7B model, slowly, while everything else swapped. That is no longer the interesting question. Quantization, speculative decoding and better metal kernels moved the bottleneck from memory capacity to memory bandwidth, and the practical consequence is that a 4B model at Q4 now answers in roughly the time it takes to read the question.

The second change is architectural. Browser extensions used to ship their own inference loop, which meant every project re-implemented model loading, keep-alive and structured output. A local engine that owns the runtime and exposes a task protocol removes that duplication: the interface extracts data, the engine routes a task, a plugin does the work. The interface never learns which model ran.

The third change is boring and important: structured output. Asking a model nicely for JSON worked about nine times out of ten. Grammar-constrained decoding makes the tenth case disappear, which is what turns a demo into something a moderator can rely on.

What has not changed is trust. Page text is untrusted input, model output is untrusted data, and neither should ever reach a shell or an innerHTML sink. The fastest way to ruin a local AI tool is to let a webpage decide what gets executed.
title: Local inference on Apple Silicon: what actually changed in 2026

items.author: ana
items.text: Bandwidth is the real limit. My M1 Pro and my M3 Max run the same 4B model, and the Max is about twice as fast, which tracks the bandwidth ratio almost exactly.

items.author: dev
items.text: Grammar-constrained output was the unlock for us. We stopped writing JSON repair code entirely.

items.author: anon
items.text: Idle unloading matters more than people think. Keeping a 4B model resident costs you battery even when nothing is asking it questions.

items.author: mod
items.text: Reminder that a plugin is a trusted local program. Read the code before you drop it in the plugins folder.
